order_note: Casey, Nov 10 (D-2591): use this week's tokens to move the build as far as possible. After a resync and claim_first, claimable tasks are tried longest remaining dependency chain first (open dependents, the task counted, gates included), kit-state order breaking ties; ordering only. Remove this key (or set "state") to go back to kit-state order. runner/__main__.py claim_order_setting and runner/cycle.py chain_lengths read it.
prefer_disjoint_crates_note: D-3082 (Nov 11, efficiency audit F2): two tasks in one app/ crate both update its CLAUDE.md, and the second to merge needs a resync (D-891). With this true, among claimable tasks of equal priority (after a resync, claim_first and the critical-path chain length) one whose app/ crates no task in flight shares is tried first; ordering only, so when every candidate shares a crate the claim is made as before and every lane still fills. Set false (or remove the key) to go back to the old order. runner/__main__.py prefer_disjoint_crates and runner/lanes.py crowded read it.
exclusive_crates_note: D-3269 (Nov 12): on November 12 nearly every resync conflict was in a crate CLAUDE.md or src/api.rs, about 1 task in 5 at five lanes. With this true the runner never claims a task that writes an app/ crate (its owned paths under app/<crate>/ and its module) already written by as many tasks in flight (IN_PROGRESS or MERGE_PENDING, any lane) as the crate's limit (crate_cap below, D-3303; 1 without it); the task itself is never counted against itself (a resync is not blocked by its own crate) and FIX-MAIN is exempt. A run whose every candidate collides ends idle: no strike, the lane stays, no refill run. prefer_disjoint_crates still orders what remains. Set false (or remove the key) to claim as before. runner/__main__.py exclusive_crates and runner/lanes.py crate_clash read it.
crate_cap_note: D-3303 (Nov 12; owner decision by Fable under Casey's standing rule, Casey: speed is the goal, quality must not decline): with exclusive_crates true, a crate may hold up to this many tasks in flight (IN_PROGRESS or MERGE_PENDING, any lane) instead of one, because at 19:31Z only 4 of 7 lanes were busy while every claimable task shared a crate with work in flight. A crate whose app/<crate>/CLAUDE.md on origin/main, counted in lines plus its tasks in flight, reaches the 120-line limit (scripts/check_code_docs.py MAX_CRATE_DOC_LINES; a missing file counts as full) still holds one. D-3082's ordering and D-3269's reservation stay: a blocked top candidate keeps the last free slot in each of its crates. Missing, malformed or below 1 reads as 1 (D-3269's hard exclusion); exclusive_crates false turns the whole rule off. Guardrail: if more than 1 merge in 5 needs a resync over the next 10 merges, or CI queues, set this back to 1 through a logged plan change. runner/__main__.py crate_cap and crate_doc_full and runner/lanes.py crate_limit read it. D-3386 (Nov 13): the guardrail tripped, 3 of the 10 merges after D-3303 (T385, T162, T351) needed a resync, each conflict in a crate CLAUDE.md, so the cap is back to 1; raise it again only through a new owner decision or a harness change that removes crate CLAUDE.md conflicts, logged as a plan change. D-3444 (Nov 13; Casey, Nov 13: "If there is anything we can do to improve token efficiency and speed up build time without impacting quality do it"): the cap is 2 again. All three resyncs that tripped D-3386 came from one commit (47b884064, D-3308) condensing the businesses, intake and quotes CLAUDE.md files while tasks there ran, rewrite conflicts rather than two tasks appending; every crate CLAUDE.md is now 32-108 lines, and cap 1 idled lanes (T312, T367 behind intake). New rule (docs/code-docs.md section 2): nobody condenses or restructures a crate CLAUDE.md while any task writing that crate is in flight; check kit/state.json on claude/kit-state first. The full-file hybrid above stays, and so does the guardrail: more than 1 merge in 5 needing a resync over the 10 merges after D-3444, or CI queuing, sets this back to 1 through a logged plan change. D-3474 (Nov 13): every crate CLAUDE.md is now a guide of at most 8,192 bytes (scripts/check_code_docs.py MAX_CRATE_DOC_BYTES, about 15 to 45 lines) with the detail in app/<crate>/NOTES.md, one entry per line and union-merged (.gitattributes), so the line count alone no longer marks a crate full; T437 makes crate_doc_full also count bytes plus 400 (CRATE_DOC_TASK_BYTES) for each task in flight and the next. The cap stays 2 and the guardrail stays.
